overview: Rise 5.99's Regen is the most configurable of the three: a ModeSetting with Normal and Ghostly, a Health threshold (default 15), a Speed burst size (default 20, maximum 300) and a Tick interval (default 1, maximum 20). The onPreMotion handler fires while ticksExisted is above 10, health is below the threshold and ticksExisted modulo the tick setting is zero; Normal sends the speed count of plain C03PacketPlayer instances, while Ghostly sends C06PacketPlayerPosLook at posY plus 1E-9 with onGround false. Every send goes through PacketUtil.sendPacket, so the bursts pass the client's normal send wrapper.

sections.p: The four settings are declared as fields and read per event. NumberSetting construction is (name, module, value, min, max, increment), so Health defaults to 15 in a 0-20 range, Speed to 20 in a 1-300 range and Tick to 1 in a 1-20 range. The ticksExisted modulo Tick gate spreads the bursts: with Tick 1 the module fires every tick, with Tick 20 it fires once per second. The Speed value is the burst size, so the default is 20 packets per triggering tick (400 per second) and the maximum setting produces 300 packets per tick (6000 per second).

Normal instantiates new C03PacketPlayer() per send: the vanilla default with onGround false and no position or rotation flags, one byte on the wire. Ghostly instantiates C06PacketPlayerPosLook with the current position, posY plus 1E-9, the current yaw and pitch and onGround false: a full position-plus-look update. The 1E-9 lift is below the 0.03 minimum-move epsilon, so the server applies the flag while discarding the coordinate delta, and the onGround false is the inverse of the classic claim, deliberately never asserting ground so it earns no fall-distance reset. The Ghostly name matches the Ghostly phase profile in the client's other movement modules.

FoodStats.onUpdate runs once per server tick and heals 1 HP per 80 ticks while foodLevel is 18 or above and shouldHeal holds; packet volume does not advance that timer on a stock server. The module's real observable behavior is the burst rate and the ground-flag pattern: Normal floods flag-only packets, Ghostly floods grounded-false position claims. The default 20 per tick already exceeds the 22 per second ceiling that rate checks enforce, and the maximum Speed setting produces a burst of 300 packets in one tick, which no rate model tolerates.

files.label: Regen.java
files.explanation:
A single handler module with four settings and one onPreMotion method. The @ModuleInfo declaration names it Regen with the description 'Regenerates your health super fast by spamming position packets'. The handler evaluates ticksExisted above 10, health below the Health setting and the modulo gate, then loops the Speed count over the selected mode's packet construction. Normal uses the flag-only default constructor; Ghostly builds a C06 with the 1E-9 lift and onGround false. There are no other handlers and no state fields, so the module is fully described by this one method.

The send path matters: PacketUtil.sendPacket routes through mc.getNetHandler().addToSendQueue, the normal queue, so the bursts are interleaved with vanilla movement traffic and reach the server in send order. The tick gate is the only pacing mechanism, and with the default Tick of 1 the module fires every tick while health is below threshold.

files.label: PacketUtil.java (send wrapper)
files.explanation:
The module's only util import. sendPacket pushes any packet into the normal outbound queue through mc.getNetHandler().addToSendQueue, and the sibling sendPacketWithoutEvent uses the queue variant that skips the client's own event pipeline. The Regen module uses sendPacket, so its bursts pass through the event pipeline like vanilla sends, which matters for modules that intercept their own traffic: nothing in this module cancels or delays its own packets.

The wrapper is shared across the Rise 5.99 combat modules, so the Regen burst shape is consistent with the rest of the client's packet usage. The distinction between the two send variants is the one design detail worth knowing: sendPacketWithoutEvent exists for packets the client must not re-observe, and Regen deliberately does not use it.

countering.label: FastHeal (health regain rate)
countering.explanation:
FastHeal enforces a 4000ms minimum interval between SATIATED regain events with a 1000ms buffer, canceling the heal from vl 10 upward when the buffer drains. The module's advertised purpose is exactly to produce heals faster than the vanilla one-per-4-seconds cadence, so every extra heal the spam triggers is cancelled before it lands. The Health threshold default of 15 HP puts the module in the same window where natural regen is active, matching the check's reason filter.

The check is packet-agnostic and reacts to the server-side heal events alone, so neither the Normal flag-only shape nor the Ghostly pos-look shape changes the outcome: any regain beyond the interval is refused. On an NCP-protected server the module degenerates into pure packet spam with no healing effect, which is why the rate check below is the one that actually ends the session.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation:
Every burst packet flows through the NCP flying queue and is scored per processed move. The window accumulator enforces a 22 per second ceiling with 500ms buckets, and the burst path flags 15 packets in a half-second bucket with a direct violation at 10. Rise's default Speed of 20 per tick is 400 per second, about 18 times the ceiling; the maximum Speed of 300 per tick is 6000 per second. Both the window accumulator and the burst bucket trip within the first second.

The Tick gate changes the cadence but not the outcome: with Tick 20 the module sends one burst of 20 packets per second, which is below the window ceiling but still trips the burst path because 20 packets land inside a single half-second bucket. The default actions cancel from vl 2 upward and escalate to a kick, so the module cannot operate on an NCP-protected server at any Speed setting.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (ground truth and vertical envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly derives ground state from the block cache, so the Ghostly mode's onGround false claim is ignored in both directions: the envelope treats the player as grounded when the ray trace agrees and does not reward the false flag, and the 1E-9 lift sits below the 0.03 minimum-move so the coordinate delta is never scored. The module therefore gets nothing from the movement layer, which is the honest measure of the mode: Ghostly's only observable effect is the packet rate.

The check still anchors the enforcement: the morePacketsSetBack location is seeded from the SurvivalFly set-back, so when the rate check fires the player is snapped to the last verified grounded position. The combination is what makes the module harmless on an NCP-protected server: the envelope keeps the ground state truthful, and the rate check carries the actual penalty.
